summary.summary: Dover ended 2025/26 with £46.5m in externally managed strategic pooled bond, multi-asset and property funds (£2.1m income in the year, a 4.57% average return) while running day-to-day cash on £55m of short-term loans borrowed from other councils. That short-term stance cost it: borrowing costs came in £894k above the original £1,091k budget as inter-authority money became scarcer and housing development drew cash. The council breached its own interest-rate-risk indicator — a 1% rate move now shifts net interest by £693k against a £500k target — and has responded by raising the 2026/27 limit to £750k rather than shrinking the exposure. All other treasury and prudential limits were complied with, and no debt rescheduling is considered worthwhile.
summary.as_of_doc: Treasury Management Year End Report for 2025/26

signals.headline: Interest-rate-risk indicator breached in 2025/26 — £693k net-interest sensitivity to a 1% rate move vs the £500k target — and the limit has been raised to £750k for 2026/27 rather than the exposure cut
signals.why: Raising the limit after a breach normalises a rate-sensitive balance sheet built on rolling short-term borrowing.

signals.headline: 2025/26 cost of borrowing rose £894k above the original £1,091k budget estimate, driven by additional short-term borrowing, reduced availability of inter-authority funds, and housing development spend
signals.why: A small district's interest line nearly doubling in-year shows how exposed the revenue budget is to short-term rates and money-market supply.

news_drafts.headline: Dover fails to recover housing repair costs, with critical audit fix delayed 18 months
news_drafts.lead: Dover District Council has recovered just £9,189 of £194,731 raised in rechargeable works orders for housing repairs over four years, a recovery rate of 4.7 per cent. The Governance Committee heard on 24 September that collection has effectively stalled: no money was recovered in 2025-26 despite £8,328 being raised, and only £220 of £1,333 raised by June 2026. A critical priority recommendation from the council's internal auditors in March 2025 to pursue recovery of outstanding orders remains unimplemented; management now plans to complete the recovery and write-off process by March 2027. The council is separately owed £722,409 for administering elections on behalf of Kent County Council and central government, though payments for these can take up to two years to arrive. Internal audit gave improving ratings to counter fraud arrangements and business rates administration, moving each from limited or reasonable assurance to reasonable or substantial.

findings.paper_title: DDC - Quarterly Internal Audit Update Report 24-09-2026
findings.headline: PartnershipOne Business Rates Reliefs and Credits audit improved from Reasonable to Substantial assurance with only one medium-priority recommendation outstanding
findings.detail: Follow-up review shows improvement from Reasonable assurance (2 medium, 4 low recommendations) to Substantial assurance. Five of six original recommendations have been closed; only 1 low-priority recommendation remains outstanding. This represents significant progress in strengthening controls over business rates administration.
findings.matters: Improved controls over business rates administration reduce revenue leakage risk and strengthen financial integrity
findings.figures: Moved from Reasonable to Substantial assurance; 6 original recommendations reduced to 1 low-priority outstanding
findings.quote: PartnershipOne Limited – Business Rates Reliefs & Credits | Reasonable | Substantial

findings.paper_title: DDC - Quarterly Internal Audit Update Report 24-09-2026
findings.headline: Counter Fraud Resilience Arrangements audit improved from Limited to Reasonable assurance, with four high-priority recommendations on track for 30 September 2026 completion
findings.detail: Follow-up review of Counter Fraud Resilience shows improvement from Limited assurance (3 critical, 6 high, 5 low recommendations) to Reasonable assurance with four high-priority recommendations remaining outstanding but on target. The four outstanding recommendations have not been escalated to committee because implementation is tracking to the 30 September 2026 deadline.
findings.matters: Strengthening fraud control systems reduces the council's exposure to financial loss from fraud and misappropriation
findings.figures: Moved from Limited to Reasonable assurance; 4 high-priority recommendations outstanding but on track
findings.quote: ** Please Note the 4 Recommendations regarding above - e) 'Counter Fraud Resilience Arrangements' have not been escalated as they are on target and due to be implemented by 30 September 2026.

findings.paper_title: DDC - Quarterly Internal Audit Update Report 24-09-2026
findings.headline: Five council services retain Limited or No assurance ratings pending follow-up reviews, including Grounds Maintenance (No assurance) and Housing Repairs and Maintenance (Limited)
findings.detail: Annex 2 identifies five services not yet followed up following initial limited or no assurance audits: CCTV, Licensing, Grounds Maintenance, Housing Repairs and Maintenance, and Performance Management. These services contain documented control gaps that remain unresolved, with follow-up work listed as work-in-progress. Grounds Maintenance audit received No assurance, the lowest rating.
findings.matters: Unresolved control weaknesses across multiple housing and operational services could allow losses, errors or compliance failures to go undetected
findings.figures: 5 services awaiting follow-up: CCTV (Substantial/Limited); Licensing (Reasonable/Limited); Grounds Maintenance (No); Housing Repairs and Maintenance (Limited); Performance Management (Limited)
findings.quote: SERVICES GIVEN LIMITED / NO ASSURANCE LEVELS YET TO BE REVIEWED

findings.paper_title: DDC - Quarterly Internal Audit Update Report 24-09-2026
findings.headline: Dover District Council is owed £722,409.77 for administering the last three elections, with central government and county council payments taking up to two years to arrive
findings.detail: Electoral Registration and Election Management audit (Substantial assurance) identified that while the council's electoral processes are well-managed, payments from Kent County Council and central government for elections administered on their behalf face significant delays. The council currently holds £722,409.77 receivable for the last three elections, typical payment cycles extend to two years, creating a material cash flow timing issue.
findings.matters: Extended payment delays on material government-owed debts materially affect council liquidity and cash flow planning
findings.figures: £722,409.77 owed for last 3 elections; up to 2 years payment delay
findings.quote: payments for these from Kent County Council and Central Government are not forthcoming and can take up to 2 years to be received. Currently Dover District Council is owed £722,409.77 for the last 3 elections carried out across the district.

findings.paper_title: DDC - Quarterly Internal Audit Update Report 24-09-2026
findings.headline: Housing rechargeable works orders totalling £194,731 have recovered only £9,189, with critical audit recommendations unimplemented for 18 months
findings.detail: The council raised £194,731.21 in rechargeable works orders over four years but recovered only £9,189.25 (4.7%). Recovery has effectively stopped in 2025-26 and 2026-27: £8,328 raised in 2025-26 generated zero recovery; £1,333 raised by June 2026 generated £220. A critical priority recommendation from March 2025 to pursue recovery of outstanding orders remains unimplemented; management's September 2026 comment notes the "recovery/write-off process remains outstanding" with revised completion pushed to March 2027.
findings.matters: Poor cash collection on services provided indicates weak receivables control and cash flow risk
findings.figures: £194,731.21 raised; £9,189.25 recovered; 2025-26: £8,327.81 raised, £0 recovered; 2026-27 (to June): £1,333.20 raised, £220 recovered
